expected_behavior: Run on docs/evals/fixtures/release-notes: copies the folder to an old_skill snapshot in the OS temp directory before reading it further, and prints the snapshot path. Prints a numbered candidate list; each item cites a slop-signal ID (SL1 to SL7, with its checklist ID where one exists), quotes the text and gives its path:line. The list contains at least: SL1/B2 quoting 'A changelog is a file that lists the changes'; SL2/B8 quoting 'Each pull request gets exactly one line'; SL3/B4 quoting 'whichever you prefer'; SL4/B9 quoting 'IMPORTANT: You MUST NEVER include' and proposing a reason in place of the shouting while keeping the chore(deps) rule; SL5/B8 quoting the repeated 'Group the entries by Conventional Commit type'; SL6/D3 quoting the trigger list in the description, marked as not rewritten and referred to skill-creator's description optimisation; SL7/B10 for the emoji in the title, the 'Overview' heading and the 'In summary' closing section. Before editing any file, prints the rule inventory of the snapshot, which lists at least the git log step, the grouping by Conventional Commit type, the output format, the chore(deps) exclusion and one line per pull request, each with its snapshot path:line. Interviews the author in numbered questions, each with a recommended answer that 'yes' accepts, and records every candidate as accepted, rejected or load-bearing before any file changes. Rewrites the skill once and leaves the frontmatter description byte-for-byte unchanged. Maps every inventory item to a path:line in the new text or to 'struck by author' with the interview answer that struck it, and states that the inventory catches lost rules but not shifted emphasis or tone. With every item mapped, prints a unified diff of snapshot against rewrite and asks before creating a branch and a pull request. When the chore(deps) rule is missing from the new text and no interview answer struck it, as in the prompt that deletes it after the rewrite, the inventory names it as unmapped with its snapshot path:line, delivers nothing (no diff as the result, no branch, commit or pull request), and asks the author to restore the rule or strike it. Run on the unpacked claude.ai copy of docs/evals/fixtures/protokoll outside any git repository: takes the snapshot without requiring, initialising or creating a repository, and scans the German text with the same signals, citing at least SL1/B2 quoting 'Ein Protokoll ist ein Dokument', SL3/B4 quoting 'ganz wie du möchtest', SL4/B9 quoting 'WICHTIG: Du DARFST NIEMALS' while keeping the phone-number rule, SL5/B8 quoting the repeated 'Ordne jeden Beschluss seinem Tagesordnungspunkt zu' and SL7/B10 for the emoji, the 'Überblick' heading and the 'Zusammenfassung' section; quotes stay in German and the rewritten text stays German, never translated. On 'yes' to deliver, creates no branch, commit or pull request; packs the rewrite with skill-creator's scripts/package_skill.py into protokoll.skill beside ~/Downloads/protokoll.zip, leaves protokoll.zip byte-for-byte unchanged, prints the unified diff and both archive paths, and tells the author to upload the new archive in claude.ai by hand and to upload the old ZIP the same way to roll back.
